examples.title: Word problems
examples.problem: At a shop, dal costs ₹40 a kg more than rice. 2 kg of rice and 3 kg of dal cost ₹420 together. Find the price of each per kg.
steps: Let rice cost r rupees a kg, so dal costs r + 40.
r = 60, so rice costs ₹60 a kg and dal costs ₹100 a kg.
examples.answer: Rice ₹60 per kg, dal ₹100 per kg

examples.title: Ages
examples.problem: The ages of a mother and her daughter add up to 50. Five years ago the mother was 7 times as old as the daughter. Find their present ages.
steps: Let the daughter be d years old now, so the mother is 50 − d.
Five years ago: (50 − d) − 5 = 7(d − 5), so 45 − d = 7d − 35.
8d = 80, so d = 10 and the mother is 40.

examples.title: Simultaneous equations
steps: Add the equations: 8x + 8y = 40, so x + y = 5.
Subtract the first from the second: 2x − 2y = −2, so x − y = −1.
Add these two results: 2x = 4, so x = 2 and y = 3.

examples.title: Consistency of a pair of equations
examples.problem: For which values of k does the system kx + 2y = 5 and 3x + y = 1 have exactly one solution?
steps: Exactly one solution needs k/3 to differ from 2/1.
k/3 = 2 only when k = 6, so every other value of k gives one solution.
At k = 6 the constants give 5/1, which differs from 2, so the lines are parallel and there is no solution.

examples.title: Integer solutions
examples.problem: How many pairs of positive integers (x, y) satisfy 5x + 3y = 64?
steps: Find one pair: x = 2 gives 3y = 54, so y = 18.
Other pairs come from adding 3 to x and taking 5 from y: (5, 13), (8, 8) and (11, 3).
The next step gives y = −2, which is not allowed. x must leave remainder 2 when divided by 3, so 2 is the smallest x.
